evidence.title: MAPS' Phase 3 Trial of MDMA-Assisted Therapy for PTSD Achieves Successful Results for Patients with Severe, Chronic PTSD

evidence.title: MDMA-assisted therapy for severe PTSD: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study (MAPP1)
A Multi-Site Phase 3 Study of MDMA-Assisted Psychotherapy for PTSD (MAPP1)

outcome.note: The sponsor topline release of 2021-05-03 reports that MAPP1, the first Phase 3 trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD (NCT03537014, MAPS PBC), met its prespecified primary endpoint: CAPS-5 total severity fell more with MDMA-assisted therapy than with placebo plus therapy, p<0.0001. Nature Medicine published the same result on 2021-05-10 (mean change -24.4 vs -13.9; d=0.91). This is a Phase 3 result on the prespecified primary efficacy endpoint, not an interim or pooled analysis. The date is the sponsor release, which precedes the publication.

event.asset: midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD: FDA treatment of the Phase 3 double-blind in its review of the application
event.title: FDA challenges the midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) Phase 3 results over an unsuccessful double-blind
event.proposition: The FDA's written action on, or review of, the midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) application for post-traumatic stress disorder cites an unsuccessful double-blind in the Phase 3 trials as a basis for not accepting the efficacy results.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of an FDA written action (complete response letter, refuse-to-file letter or other written FDA communication the sponsor discloses), an FDA review document posted on Drugs@FDA, or an FDA advisory committee briefing document that names failure or loss of the double-blind (functional unblinding, or expectancy bias from unblinding) in the Phase 3 trials of midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD, under any sponsor name, as a reason the efficacy results are not adequate for approval. A document that only asks a question about blinding, without treating it as a deficiency, does not count. Resolution source: Drugs@FDA (action letters and review documents) with the FDA advisory committee materials page. FALSE when the FDA approves the application with no such finding, or when no such document exists at the deadline.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA (action letters, review documents); FDA advisory committee materials

readings: 'Our final results will not be challenged on the basis of an unsuccessful double-blind' = the FDA does not cite unblinding as a deficiency of the Phase 3 efficacy results; the forecaster denies the proposition.
Any sponsor name (MAPS, MAPS PBC or a successor) counts; the entry is on the asset.
Distinct from E-0027 (safety data cited in a non-approval) and from E-0001 (approval): this event is about the stated basis of the FDA's assessment, not the approval decision.

evidence.title: Complete Response Letter, NDA 215455 (midomafetamine capsules), Lykos Therapeutics
evidence.publisher: US Food and Drug Administration (openFDA CRL release)

evidence.title: Lykos Therapeutics Announces Complete Response Letter for Midomafetamine Capsules for PTSD
FDA Briefing Document, NDA 215455 midomafetamine, Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee Meeting

outcome.note: The FDA complete response letter for NDA 215455 names functional unblinding as part of the basis for not accepting the efficacy results. Deficiency 3 says prior midomafetamine use made participants 'more likely to recognize the effects of midomafetamine (i.e., leading to functional unblinding) and anticipate a treatment benefit', and concludes: 'These limitations impact the interpretability of MAPP1 and MAPP2 and, together with failure of MPLONG to provide evidence of a durable treatment effect, preclude the ability to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness.' Date is the issue date the sponsor disclosed; the letter's electronic signature reads 08/08/2024. The 2024-06-04 advisory committee briefing document already called functional unblinding a problem for interpreting efficacy, but stopped short of a deficiency finding.

MDMA-assisted Massed Prolonged Exposure for PTSD (NCT06117306), Phase 3, sponsor Healing Breakthrough; actual start 2024-10-25

outcome.note: Criterion (a) is met. The first interventional Phase 3 MDMA-for-PTSD trial with a sponsor outside the MAPS programme is NCT05979844 (Dr. Leslie Morland, VA San Diego), actual start 2023-10-06; it administers MDMA and produces its own data, with Resilient (ex-Lykos) only a collaborator supplying drug. Three later independent records confirm the pattern: NCT06117306 (Healing Breakthrough, 2024-10-25), NCT06394284 (Herzog Hospital, 2024-02-18) and NCT07118839 (VA ORD, Phase 2/3, 2026-05-18). NCT06189027 (USC, start 2018-11-20) is excluded: it is a saliva biomarker add-on to the MAPS trial MAPP1 and gives no drug itself.

Recognify Life Sciences Provides Update on Phase 2b Trial of Inidascamine in Patients with Cognitive Impairment Associated with Schizophrenia

outcome.note: Recognify Life Sciences (atai) reported topline results on 2025-07-25. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2b trial of inidascamine (formerly RL-007) in 242 patients with cognitive impairment associated with schizophrenia did not meet its primary endpoint, the MCCB neurocognitive composite score at week 6, with numerical improvement in both active arms. This is the first public report of the primary-endpoint result, not an interim or blinded update, so it fixes the date. The direction of the result does not matter under the criterion.
